title: Noetherian nodal families: dualizing module equals the adjunction line, compatibly with base change
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension] in which every nonsmooth closed point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Assume that $X$ is covered by factorizations $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to T$ with $P$ open in $\mathbf A^n_T$ and $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $n-1$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Call such $f$ admissible. Let $\omega_{X/T}$, with its base-change comparisons $b^*\omega_{X/T}\simeq\omega_{X'/T'}$ and its comparisons along isomorphisms of families, be the relative dualizing module of [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing], and let $K_{X/T}$, with its base-change comparisons, be the adjunction line of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] for $d=1$; for a $T$-isomorphism $\varphi:X''\to X$ of admissible families, $\varphi^*K_{X/T}\simeq K_{X''/T}$ is the comparison obtained by composing presentations with $\varphi$. Then there is, for every admissible $f$, an isomorphism of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] $\theta_f:\omega_{X/T}\to K_{X/T}$ with the following properties. (1) For every morphism $a:T'\to T$ with $T'$ Noetherian, with $X'=X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $b:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to T'$ (which is again admissible), the composite $b^*\omega_{X/T}\xrightarrow{b^*\theta_f}b^*K_{X/T}\simeq K_{X'/T'}$ equals $b^*\omega_{X/T}\simeq\omega_{X'/T'}\xrightarrow{\theta_{f'}}K_{X'/T'}$, module pullback being [def-pc-module-pullback]. (2) For every $T$-isomorphism $\varphi:X''\to X$ of admissible families, $\theta_{f\varphi}$ corresponds to $\varphi^*\theta_f$ under the two comparisons along $\varphi$. No choice of factorization enters $\theta_f$.

proof.text: Work locally with a presentation from the hypothesis and put $c=n-1$, $C_i=I/I^2$, $V_i=i^*\Omega^1_{P/T}$ and $D_i=(\bigwedge^c C_i)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV_i$. The regular equations are Koszul-regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] gives their classes as a conormal basis of rank $c$. Thus all hypotheses of the normalized Koszul comparison hold, including when $c=0$. By [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing], $\omega_f=H^{-1}(f^!\mathcal O_T)$ is invertible and $f^!\mathcal O_T\simeq\omega_f[1]$. Properness, flatness, finite presentation and the geometric nodal assumptions are exactly its hypotheses; connectedness is unnecessary.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] to identify $f^!\mathcal O_T$ locally with $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/T})[n]$, retaining its $B$-action and specified ordered refinement comparisons. On ambient-open presentations use restriction of these models. Since $n-1=c$, its degree $-1$ is the top Ext in degree $c$. The inverse of the normalized map in [lem-trf-lci-adjunction-top-ext] therefore defines a local module isomorphism $\theta_i:\omega_f|_{U_i}\simeq D_i$. The sign is fixed by that node's formula: its top-Ext map is the inverse of $H^c(\rho_i)$, not an independently chosen generator. All maps are module maps with the natural quotient action.

source.place: Tags 0E2W, 0E2Y, 0E2Z, 0E4P; dualizing.tex Tags 0BZR and 0BZJ, normalized polynomial models; Tag 0BQZ, signed Koszul duality.

proof.text: The transition assertion of [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] says that the maps $\rho_i[n]$ change between presentations by $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)[1]$. By [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] these are exactly the specified transitions of the adjunction line $K_f$. Hence the maps $\omega_f|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\theta_i}D_i\to K_f|_{U_i}$ agree on every overlap. Glue them and their inverses by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1), obtaining $\theta_f:\omega_f\simeq K_f$. No derived morphisms are glued here. The same transition identity shows that refining or replacing any presentation gives the same local module maps, hence the same $\theta_f$.

source.place: Tags 0E2W, 0E2Y, 0E2Z, 0E4P; dualizing.tex Tags 0BZR and 0BZJ, normalized polynomial models; Tag 0BQZ, signed Koszul duality.

proof.text: For $a:T'\to T$ with $T'$ Noetherian, properness, flatness and finite presentation persist by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Let $s'\in T'$ lie over $s\in T$. Reassociating fibre products, the geometric fibre $X'_{\bar s'}$ is the fibre of $f$ at the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s')}\to T$, a base change of $X_s$ along $\kappa(s)\to\overline{\kappa(s')}$; so is $X_{\bar s}$. By [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change], applied to both, every local dimension of $X'_{\bar s'}$ equals that of $X_s$ at the image point, hence that of $X_{\bar s}$, namely one; thus $X'_{\bar s'}$ is pure of dimension one. It is nonempty since $X_s\neq\emptyset$ and a nonzero algebra over a field stays nonzero after a field extension. The completed local nodal condition is assumed at every algebraically closed $\Omega\to T$, in particular here; so [lem-trf-nodal-points-reduced-algebraically-closed] makes $X'_{\bar s'}$ reduced. By [lem-trf-flat-lci-presentation-base-change] the pulled-back equations are regular in the local ring of $P'$ at every point of $U'$ and are Koszul-regular on the ambient charts, with the same conormal rank $c$ and differential rank $n$. Over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset T'$ with $R'$ Noetherian, the affine opens of $P'$ have finite type coordinate rings over $R'$, which are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] gives a principal neighbourhood, still open in $\mathbf A^n_{T'}$, on which the equations form a regular sequence generating $I'$. These are the required presentations; thus $f'$ is admissible and steps 1--3 apply to it.

source.place: Tags 0E2W, 0E2Y, 0E2Z, 0E4P; dualizing.tex Tags 0BZR and 0BZJ, normalized polynomial models; Tag 0BQZ, signed Koszul duality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-duality-polynomial-base-change]. Both bases are locally Noetherian and $f$ is separated because it is proper. Its proper-case clause identifies the given dualizing-module comparison with the degree $-1$ map on the polynomial models. On a regular presentation take the finite free Koszul resolution $F$. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] its extension is the Koszul resolution for the pulled-back equations (exact by step 4). On each ordered wedge basis the Hom map sends $h\otimes r'$ to the functional $z\otimes s'\mapsto r's'(h(z)\otimes1)$. Thus on the top dual wedge it sends the dual of $\bar h_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar h_c$, tensored with the ordered coordinate volume form, to the same pulled-back tensor, with the same sign. By [lem-trf-lci-adjunction-top-ext] this is the normalization defining $\theta_i$. By [lem-trf-flat-lci-presentation-base-change] and [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] it is also the specified adjunction-line comparison. The two composites in (1) therefore agree on these local generators, hence as module maps on each chart and globally. This argument allows nonflat $a$; only flatness of $f$ was used.

source.place: Tags 0E2W, 0E2Y, 0E2Z, 0E4P; dualizing.tex Tags 0BZR and 0BZJ, normalized polynomial models; Tag 0BQZ, signed Koszul duality.

proof.text: For a $T$-isomorphism $\varphi:X''\to X$, use on $X''$ the presentations on $X$ composed with $\varphi$. The ambient Koszul resolutions, ordered equations and volume forms are the same, with their quotient modules transported by the induced ring isomorphism. The isomorphism naturality in [lem-sfb-relative-duality-polynomial-base-change] identifies the given dualizing comparison with this transport. The presentation description of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] identifies the adjunction comparison with the same transport of $D_i$. The normalized top-Ext map of step 2 is unchanged on every ordered basis. Therefore $\theta_{f\varphi}=\varphi^*\theta_f$ under the stated comparisons locally and hence globally. Together with steps 3 and 5 this proves both clauses and presentation independence.
